conflict_resolutions.EMPTY_CATALOG_NOTE_DOES_NOT_ESTABLISH_CU: The catalog observation for EO 7946 has an empty note, so it neither shows that the order ended nor that it continues. I did not use it. The status rests on the order's own wording (the limit applies during the last six months of the calendar year 1938) and on the held text of EO 8051, which states that EO 7946 covered July 1 to December 31, 1938; the bounded searches found no extension.

notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: Executive Order 7946 (August 9, 1938; 3 FR 1965) limits Canadian red cedar shingle imports admitted to entry during the last six months of the calendar year 1938 to 864,881 squares. The limit is confined to that period by the order's own words and expired on December 31, 1938 (inclusive; the exclusive reading is January 1, 1939). The basis record is the held text of EO 8051 (February 15, 1939; 4 FR 959), which recites that EO 7946 covered July 1 to December 31, 1938 and sets a new limit for the first six months of 1939; it confirms the period but does not itself revoke EO 7946, and the ending rests on the own terms of the original. The EO 8051 sentence that terminates an order on termination of the Canadian trade agreement ends EO 8051, not EO 7946. No held source extends or revives EO 7946. It has no operative force on 2026-10-14.
